newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shrs end strong, Telebras soars.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shrs end strong, Telebras soars.

text.p: Brazilian stocks closed strong on Thursday in heavy trade of Telebras, which reached a surprising 100.60 reais ahead of next Monday's options expiry, brokers said.
The Bovespa index of the 49 most traded shares ended 1.09 percent higher at 87,649 points.
Market turnover totalled 1.16 billion reais ($1.1 billion), the bolsa's highest volume since September 1994, according to the Sao Paulo Stock Exchange (Bovespa).
Telebras stocks and options accounted for over 60 percent of today's trade.
The bolsa usually trades over $1.0 billion only in options expiry dates.
"Discounting the options settlements dates, today's turnover was the highest since September 1994," a bourse spokeswoman said.

Traders attributed the bourse's strong performance partly to players who rushed to the market to cover short positions as Telebras preferred, which had risen over six percent Wednesday to adjust to its ADR prices in New York, continued to surge. They noted Telebras at 100.60 reais caught many players by surprise.

"The options game started with traders betting on Telebras at strike price of 88 reais to be exercised. Now Telebras at 100 reais has chances to be exercised," said an analyst, adding that the futures index settlement also helped to bolster the market.
Firm Wall Street stock prices and an absence of news that could prevent the bolsa from moving higher were also behind the bourse's rally, traders said.
Analysts said local stocks could continue rising Friday, but volatility is likely to increase as tomorrow will be the last session before the options settlement.
They noted the bolsa's volume could remain high, particularly if players decide not to wait until Monday to exercise their options.
Today only 1.3 million reais in options were exercised.
